observations: White game console with a vertical orientation and a disc drive slot.
The console features a horizontal slit across the side panels, characteristic of the PlayStation 5 Slim model.
One white DualSense-style controller is positioned in front of the console.
Watermark 'POSTED ON JIJI ABIODUN JAMES' is visible on both images.
Background shows a framed '2014 Forest Hills Drive' album cover and a light-colored wall.
The console appears to be in good cosmetic condition from the exterior angles shown.

claims.evidence: The exterior looks well-maintained in the photos, but internal dust, port wear, or fine scratches cannot be confirmed without close-ups.
The physical design in photo 0 and 1, specifically the split side plates, is unique to the Slim revision of the PlayStation 5.
A controller is visible in both photo 0 and photo 1.

risks.risk: The console may not power on or output a video signal.
risks.proof: A video showing the console booting to the main dashboard and launching a game.

risks.risk: The disc drive may be faulty or unable to read discs.
risks.proof: A video of a game disc being inserted, recognized by the system, and ejected.

risks.risk: The console may be banned from the PlayStation Network (PSN).
risks.proof: A photo or video showing the console successfully logged into a PSN account on the home screen.

risks.risk: The controller may have analog stick drift or unresponsive buttons.
risks.proof: A video of the controller being used to navigate menus or a gameplay clip showing responsive inputs.

proof_requests: Video of the console powering on, connecting to a TV, and loading a game disc.
Photo of the model and serial number sticker (usually on the bottom or rear).
Photo of the rear ports (HDMI, power, USB) to check for physical damage.
Video demonstrating the controller's functionality in a game or system menu.
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as a PS5 Slim with a disc drive. It can be priced at its worst-case value (non-functional) until proof of operation is provided.
